statement: The finitely Y-convex functions are dense in the space of Y-convex functions: closure(FC^Y(X)) = C^Y(X).
assumptions: X and nonempty Y are compact subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces
the surplus kernel Phi has a shared finite Lipschitz constant on X x Y
f equals its Y-X biconjugate by membership in C^Y(X)
the closure is taken in the uniform norm
quantifiers: For every epsilon > 0 and every f in C^Y(X), there is a finite Y~ subset Y and g in C^{Y~}(X) with ||f-g||_infinity < epsilon. Proposition 1 proves the stronger ordering: for every epsilon there is one finite Y~ that works for every f.
